problems: dude.json (LigUnity main 8ae35edb) maps CSF1R to P11362, which is FGFR1's UniProt ID (CSF1R is P07333), so CSF1R is scored with the FGFR1 sequence; left unchanged, since the published numbers come from the same file

test_task.py prints per-target AUC and BEDROC to 4 decimals, so the means of those per_target columns differ from the logged means in the 6th decimal; EF is printed in full and its means match exactly
The DUD-E log is missing its exit-code and end-time lines (those commands were not run); the run printed every mean and the process ended normally, and the end time 00:31:22 is the log's last write

scripts/download_data.sh skips any file that is already non-empty, so an interrupted download is never resumed or replaced; the slow DEKOIS_2.0x.zip (figshare, about 200 KB/s) finished in one go and its md5 was checked

scripts/download_data.sh does not fetch test_datasets/FEP (fep_labels.json, lmdbs/), which DATA.md names as the FEP source; taken from LigUnity at 8ae35edb. The bench/ CSVs test_fep_target reads for ACC/AUC are not published, so ACC/AUC are NaN; Pearson r and Spearman rho are unaffected (as the paper states, p. 46)

The released DEKOIS_2.0x LMDBs hold fewer than the 1,240 molecules (40 actives + 1,200 decoys) per target that DEKOIS 2.0 defines for 36 of the 81 targets; 11betahsd1, 17betahsd1 and sars-hcov also lack 3, 1 and 1 actives. Scored as released; the counts are in per_target_DEKOIS.csv
The DUD-E CSV counts 22,800 actives over the 102 targets, against 22,886 in the DUD-E release; scored as released
Table A13 (p. 47) also reports a 6-target scaffold-level DEKOIS subset but does not name the targets, so it is not compared
The paper's Table 2 caption says five runs, while Table A16 gives n=4 for the multi-seed SP numbers (EF@1% 47.99 +- 0.39); the gate uses the seed-1 number of Table 1

A2 used 1.48 GPU-hours on the RTX 3060 (DUD-E 0.53, LIT-PCBA 0.90, DEKOIS 0.04, FEP 0.002), over the 1 GPU-hour checkpoint-A budget; recorded here rather than raised separately, since the overrun is small
